title: Fruit and vegetable smoothie with dairy

content.title: About
content.content: Fruit and vegetable smoothie with dairy is a drink made from fresh fruits, vegetables and dairy ingredients (milk, yogurt, kefir). It combines the natural sweetness of fruit, the nutrients of vegetables and the probiotics of dairy, providing a light and tasty way to obtain vitamins and minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Smoothies became popular in the 1970s in the United States as part of the health‑food movement.
Adding dairy improves the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins A, D, E and K from fruits and vegetables.
Smoothies can be made with any combination of fruits and vegetables, allowing endless flavor and nutrition variations.
When stored properly, a smoothie retains most of its vitamins for 24–48 hours.
In many countries smoothies are commonly served in health‑food cafés and fitness centers.

items.title: Rich in vitamins C and A
items.content: Fruits and vegetables in the smoothie provide abundant vitamin C and beta‑carotene, supporting immunity and vision.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fermented dairy supplies probiotics that promote a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Source of calcium and protein
items.content: Milk and yogurt deliver calcium and complete protein, essential for bones and muscles.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Phytonutrients from berries and leafy greens act as antioxidants, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The high water content of a smoothie helps maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance should use lactose‑free or plant‑based milk alternatives.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Very sweet fruits can raise the drink’s glycemic index; balancing with vegetables is recommended.

items.title: Allergy to individual ingredients
items.content: Allergies to berries, nuts or dairy require omission of the offending component.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Citrus fruits may irritate a sensitive stomach; those with acid reflux should choose milder options.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the smoothie cold in a glass or bottle. It works well as a breakfast, a post‑workout snack, or a refreshing drink any time of day. For extra texture and flavor, add chia seeds, nuts or a drizzle of honey.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared smoothie in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. For longer storage, freeze individual portions and thaw them in the fridge before drinking.
